# Disagreement Log — MMT Section 4 (4QMMT Section B continued: Dogs, Mixtures, Blind/Deaf, Liquid Streams)

## Summary
- **Total disagreements:** 15
- **Section:** B continued
- **Nature:** Halakhic terminology, proof-text formatting, disability exclusion language, purity concepts

---

### Disagreement 1 — Line 4:1: "eat" vs. "gnaw on"
- **EMET:** "might-eat" (literal of 'akhal)
- **LOGOS:** "might eat" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "might gnaw on" (dynamic, vivid)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "might eat" — 'akhal simply means "eat." PNEUMA's "gnaw on" adds specificity not present in the Hebrew.

### Disagreement 2 — Line 4:3: "camp of holiness" vs. "holy camp" vs. "sacred camp"
- **EMET:** "camp of-holiness" (Hebrew construct order)
- **LOGOS:** "camp of holiness" (preserves construct)
- **PNEUMA:** "holy camp" / "sacred camp" (English adjective order)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "camp of holiness" — preserves the Hebrew construct machaneh ha-qodesh, which emphasizes that holiness is the defining quality of the camp.

### Disagreement 3 — Line 4:5: "head" vs. "chief" vs. "foremost"
- **EMET:** "head of-the-camps" (literal of rosh)
- **LOGOS:** "chief of the camps" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "foremost of the camps" (dynamic)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "chief of the camps" — "chief" conveys primacy. EMET's "head" is too literal; PNEUMA's "foremost" is acceptable but "chief" is more standard.

### Disagreement 4 — Line 4:6: "holy seed" vs. "holy line"
- **EMET:** "holy seed" (literal of zera' qodesh)
- **LOGOS:** "holy seed" (formal, following Ezra 9:2)
- **PNEUMA:** "holy line" (dynamic, modernized)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "holy seed" — the phrase zera' qodesh from Ezra 9:2 is a technical theological term. "Line" loses the biological metaphor central to the author's argument.

### Disagreement 5 — Line 4:7: Proof-text formatting
- **EMET:** No quotation marks around biblical citations
- **LOGOS:** Quotation marks around "You shall not sow..."
- **PNEUMA:** "Scripture says:" plus quotation marks
- **SOPHIA ruling:** Quotation marks without "Scripture says" — LOGOS format. The citations are clearly marked as quotations, and adding "Scripture says" is interpretive.

### Disagreement 6 — Line 4:9: "two kinds of thread" vs. "mixed fabric" vs. "two different materials"
- **EMET:** "two-kinds-of-thread" (literal of sha'atnez concept)
- **LOGOS:** "mixed fabric" (standard rendering)
- **PNEUMA:** "two different materials" (explanatory)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "mixed fabric" — the standard English rendering of the kilayim prohibition on textiles. Concise and well-understood.

### Disagreement 7 — Line 4:10: "be wary of" vs. "guard against"
- **EMET:** "to-be-wary of-any-mixture" (literal)
- **LOGOS:** "to guard against any forbidden mixture" (formal, adds "forbidden")
- **PNEUMA:** "guard against forbidden mixtures" (dynamic)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "to guard against any forbidden mixture" — LOGOS's addition of "forbidden" is justified by context (the text concerns prohibited mixtures specifically).

### Disagreement 8 — Line 4:11: "profane" vs. "common"
- **EMET:** "the profane" (literal of chol)
- **LOGOS:** "the profane" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "what is common" (dynamic)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "the profane" — in the binary holy/profane, "profane" is the standard opposite of "holy" in biblical translation.

### Disagreement 9 — Line 4:13: "walks in darkness" vs. "groping in the dark"
- **EMET:** "walks in-darkness" (literal)
- **LOGOS:** "walks in darkness" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "groping in the dark" (dynamic, vivid)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "walks in darkness" — the standard biblical metaphor. PNEUMA's "groping" adds a visual element not present in the text.

### Disagreement 10 — Line 4:16: "practice the law" vs. "observe the law" vs. "keep the law"
- **EMET:** "practice the law" (literal of la'asot)
- **LOGOS:** "observe the law" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "keep the law" (dynamic)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "observe the law" — standard formal English for Torah observance. All three are valid but "observe" carries the appropriate register.

### Disagreement 11 — Line 4:17: "careful" vs. "vigilant" vs. "taking proper care"
- **EMET:** "are not careful" (literal)
- **LOGOS:** "are not vigilant" (formal, intensified)
- **PNEUMA:** "without taking proper care" (dynamic, restructured)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "are not careful" — EMET's simple rendering is adequate. LOGOS's "vigilant" elevates the register unnecessarily.

### Disagreement 12 — Line 4:20: "we say" vs. "we maintain" vs. "our position is"
- **EMET:** "we say" (literal of 'anu omerim)
- **LOGOS:** "we maintain" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "our position is" (dynamic, legalistic)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "we say" — the Hebrew is simply 'anu omerim ("we say"). This is a technical halakhic formula that should be rendered directly.

### Disagreement 13 — Line 4:20: "have no purity" vs. "have no power to purify"
- **EMET:** "have no purity" (literal of ein bahem taharah)
- **LOGOS:** "possess no purity" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "have no power to purify" (dynamic, interpretive)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "possess no purity" — the text says the streams themselves lack purity, not that they lack purifying power. PNEUMA's rendering subtly changes the legal argument.

### Disagreement 14 — Line 4:21: "one moisture" vs. "a single moisture" vs. "one connected body of liquid"
- **EMET:** "one moisture — one liquid" (literal doublet)
- **LOGOS:** "a single moisture — one continuous liquid" (formal with clarifying adjective)
- **PNEUMA:** "one connected body of liquid" (dynamic, concrete)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "a single moisture — one continuous liquid" — LOGOS's rendering preserves the doublet structure while adding "continuous" to clarify the halakhic point about unbroken liquid connection.

### Disagreement 15 — Line 4:23: "dwelling of His Presence" vs. "God's own dwelling presence"
- **EMET:** "dwelling of-His-presence" (literal of mishkan shekhinato)
- **LOGOS:** "dwelling of His Presence" (formal, capitalized)
- **PNEUMA:** "God's own dwelling presence" (dynamic, explicit subject)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "dwelling of His Presence" — "Presence" capitalized as a theological concept (shekhinah). PNEUMA's expansion to "God's own" is unnecessary when the pronoun suffices.
